editorial:
Imagine coming home after two years in the USA only to find out your dad is about to sell the family horse farm. That is exactly what happens to Monika in this cozy 1959 romance. You get a great mix of family drama and old-school charm, set against the backdrop of a fancy equestrian club. The vibe is very classic, focusing on a stubborn father who has a massive grudge against his neighbors. Things get really messy when Monika falls head over heels for the son of the very man her father hates most. It is your typical forbidden love story, but the setting makes it feel special.

You will probably love the chemistry between the young leads, though the pacing feels a bit slow by today's standards. The highlight is definitely the annual Hubertusjagd hunt, where all the tension finally boils over into a big confrontation. If you enjoy stories about overcoming family pride for love, you should definitely give this a try.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head during the big hunt. The tension between the two fathers peaks, but the love between Monika and her boyfriend proves too strong to ignore. After a dramatic encounter in the woods, the fathers finally realize that their petty rivalry is hurting their children. They shake hands and make peace, which saves the stud farm from being sold. Monika and her partner get their happy ending together as the family feud officially ends.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic romance and stories about horses.
